html:
Tufan is the Chinese name for the Tibetan Empire, which ruled the Tibetan Plateau and much of Central Asia from about 618 to 842. The map shows it around 700.

Songtsen Gampo united the plateau and took in Zhangzhung in the west. He married princesses from Nepal and from the Tang dynasty, and Tibetans date their writing, the Tibetan script, and the Jokhang temple to his reign. Around 700 the empire was fighting the Tang for the oasis towns of the Tarim Basin and had conquered the Tuyuhun kingdom near Qinghai Lake.

The empire peaked under Trisong Detsen. His armies briefly took the Tang capital Chang'an in 763, and he built Samye, the first Buddhist monastery in Tibet. A treaty with the Tang in 821 fixed the border. After the king Langdarma was killed in 842, the empire broke up.
sum: Tufan is the Chinese name for the Tibetan Empire, which ruled the Tibetan Plateau and much of Central Asia from about 618 to 842. The map shows it around 700.
